extracted.intended_audience: sovereigns, rulers, statesmen, lawmakers, and students of political theory
extracted.subtask_description: Normative guidance for the sovereign representative and the structure/practices a commonwealth must adopt to preserve safety, order, and prosperity. Covers sovereign rights, lawmaking, taxation, education of subjects, punishments/rewards, and administrative choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid division between civil and spiritual power
rubrics_metrics.description: When therefore these two Powers oppose one another, the Common-wealth cannot but be in great danger of Civill warre, and Dissolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not permit the Civill and Ghostly powers to claim equal supremacy; one must be subordinate to the other (or there will be impossible commands and likely civil war). Hobbes uses the epilepsy analogy to show how opposing spirits/powers can convulse the body politic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mixed government dividing sovereign functions
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Power of levying mony...has depended on a generall Assembly; the Power of conduct and command...on one man; and the Power of making Lawes...on the accidentall consent of a third...it is not one independent Common-wealth, but three independent Factions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not split the nutritive (taxation), motive (command), and rational (lawmaking) faculties among independent persons/bodies; such division creates factions and weakens the commonwealth's unity and nourishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain capacity to raise money (public finance readiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The difficulty of raising Mony...especially in the approach of warre...the Soveraign...contracteth it selfe as long as it can, and when it cannot longer, struggles with the people by strategems of Law...and being put often to these extremities...reduceth the people to their due temper; or else the Common-wealth must perish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure mechanisms to procure funds quickly in emergencies; inability to raise money endangers the state (compared to an ague where circulation is obstructed). Prepare legal and institutional means to supply public treasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent monopolies and abuses of revenue farming
rubrics_metrics.description: There is sometimes...a Disease...when the Treasure of the Common-wealth...is gathered together in too much abundance, in one, or a few private men, by Monopolies, or by Farmes of the Publique Revenues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid concentrating public revenue or revenue-collection in the hands of a few (monopolies, farmed revenues), which inflames and harms the body politic (likened to pleurisy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against popular ambitious subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: The Popularity of a potent Subject...is a dangerous Disease; because the people...are drawn away from their obedience to the Lawes, to follow a man, of whose vertues, and designes they have no knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for and restrain popular leaders whose flattery and reputation can seduce the people (example: Julius Caesar). Treat such ambition as a form of rebellion and a threat to sovereign authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit excessive urban power and multitude of corporations
rubrics_metrics.description: The immoderate greatnesse of a Town...and the great number of Corporations; which are as it were many lesser Common-wealths in the bowels of a greater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large towns or many autonomous corporations can act as independent commonwealths within the state and should be regulated to prevent internal fragmentation (compared to worms in the entrails).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict liberty of disputing against absolute power
rubrics_metrics.description: The Liberty of Disputing against absolute Power, by pretenders to Politicall Prudence...are perpetually medling with the Fundamentall Lawes, to the molestation of the Common-wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit the freedom of agents who habitually dispute or undermine the foundations of sovereign authority; false doctrines and endless disputation destabilize the polity (likened to ascarides/worms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereign's duty: procure safety and lawful contentments of life
rubrics_metrics.description: The OFFICE of the Soveraign...consisteth in the end...the procuration of the Safety Of The People...not meant a bare Preservation, but also all other Contentments of life, which every man by lawfull Industry, without danger, or hurt to the Common-wealth, shall acquire to himselfe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sovereign must secure both protection from harm and the conditions for lawful prosperity; this obligation is to the law of nature and accountability to God.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide public instruction and make/execute good laws
rubrics_metrics.description: This is intended should be done...by a generall Providence, contained in publique Instruction, both of Doctrine, and Example; and in the making, and executing of good Lawes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address citizen welfare through public education and clear, enforceable laws rather than individualized interventions; use instruction to shape obedience and understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain essential rights of sovereignty (do not relinquish them)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the Office of the Soveraign, to maintain those Rights entire; and consequently against his duty...to transferre to another, or to lay from himselfe any of them...supreme Judicature; or of making Warre, or Peace...of levying Mony, and Souldiers...of appointing Teachers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sovereign must keep essential prerogatives (judgment, war/peace, taxation, appointment of officers/teachers). Relinquishing them risks dissolution of the commonwealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach subjects the grounds/reasons for sovereign rights
rubrics_metrics.description: It is against his duty, to let the people be ignorant, or mis-in-formed of the grounds, and reasons of those his essentiall Rights; because thereby men are easie to be seduced, and drawn to resist him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicly and truthfully instruct citizens on why sovereign rights exist; ignorance invites sedition and misunderstanding of laws and punishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach subjects not to desire change of government
rubrics_metrics.description: They are to be taught, First, that they ought not to be in love with any forme of Government they see in their neighbour Nations...nor to desire change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instill that prosperity depends on obedience and concord, not the nominal form of government; discouraging envy of other systems helps maintain stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach subjects not to adhere to popular men over sovereign
rubrics_metrics.description: They are to be taught...that they ought not to be led with admiration of the vertue of any of their fellow Subjects...nor of any Assembly (except the Soveraign Assembly) so as to deferre to them any obedience...appropriate to the Soveraign onely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure citizens understand that honor and obedience appropriate to the sovereign should not be transferred to individuals or subordinate assemblies; influence must be conveyed only through sovereign authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach subjects not to dispute or speak evil of sovereign representative
rubrics_metrics.description: They ought to be informed, how great fault it is, to speak evill of the Soveraign Representative...or to argue and dispute his Power, or any way to use his Name irreverently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discouraging contemptuous speech or public argument against the sovereign preserves obedience and the commonwealth's safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set aside days/times for public instruction of duties and laws
rubrics_metrics.description: It is necessary that some such times be determined, wherein they may assemble together...hear those their Duties told them, and the Positive Lawes...read and expounded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular communal instruction (e.g., Sabbath-like assemblies) is required so citizens remember duties and the laws' reasons; use prayer/praise as context if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach filial obedience and honour to parents
rubrics_metrics.description: They should be obedient to them, whilest they are under their tuition; and not onely so, but that also afterwards...they acknowledge the benefit of their education, by externall signes of honour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote respect for parents as a civic duty linked to earlier forms of paternal sovereignty and social stability (aligned with the fifth commandment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach justice: abstain from violence, fraud, and corruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Soveraign Ought to cause Justice to be taught, which (consisting in taking from no man what is his) is as much as to say, to cause men to be taught not to deprive their Neighbour by violence, or fraud...and shew the evill consequences of false Judgement, by corruption either of Judges or Witnesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education in justice should cover personal nonviolence, protection of conjugal honour, and the harms of corrupted judgments; offences against private persons require restitution or consent for pardon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administer equal justice and equal taxation
rubrics_metrics.description: The safety of the People, requireth...that Justice be equally administred to all degrees of People...To Equall Justice, appertaineth also the Equall imposition of Taxes; the equality whereof dependeth not on the Equality of riches, but on the Equality of the debt, that every man oweth to the Common-wealth for his defence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justice and taxation must be applied without favoritism; tax equality is measured by equal debt for defense (suggesting consumption-based imposition rather than simple wealth metrics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide public charity for those unable to maintain themselves
rubrics_metrics.description: Whereas many men, by accident unevitable, become unable to maintain themselves by their labour; they ought not to be left to the Charity of private persons; but to be provided for...by the Lawes of the Common-wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sovereign must ensure legal provisions for the impotent/helpless rather than relying solely on private charity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent idleness; encourage arts and settle population
rubrics_metrics.description: They are to be forced to work; and...there ought to be such Lawes, as may encourage all manner of Arts; as Navigation, Agriculture, Fishing, and all manner of Manifacture...the multitude of poor...to be transplanted into Countries not sufficiently inhabited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enact policies to compel able-bodied to productive labor, promote industries, and manage surplus population via colonization or settlement rather than extermination; war is the last remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good laws must be necessary and perspicuous
rubrics_metrics.description: A good Law is that, which is Needfull, for the Good Of The People, and withall Perspicuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laws should only regulate what is necessary to protect people from harm; they should be accompanied by a declaration of causes/motives and be short and significant to avoid ambiguity and litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply punishments to correct, not to revenge; calibrate severity
rubrics_metrics.description: The end of punishing is not revenge...but correction...the severest Punishments are to be inflicted for those Crimes, that are of most Danger to the Publique...Crimes of Infirmity...there is place many times for Lenity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punish leaders and teachers of commotions more severely than the poor seduced; reserve lenity for crimes arising from provocation, fear, or ignorance; avoid punishing ignorance that stems from poor instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply rewards to benefit the commonwealth; avoid buying off ambition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office...to apply his Rewards alwayes so, as there may arise from them benefit to the Common-wealth...To buy with Mony, or Preferment, from a Popular ambitious Subject, to be quiet...has nothing of the nature of Reward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rewards to encourage genuine service with minimal public expense; do not use rewards to bribe or pacify ambitious agitators, as that encourages more ambition and damages the state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose counsellors who are able and unlikely to gain from disorder
rubrics_metrics.description: The most able Counsellours, are they that have least hope of benefit by giving evill Counsell, and most knowledge of those things that conduce to the Peace, and Defence of the Common-wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select advisers who lack incentives to promote public trouble (e.g., not indebted or seeking advantage) and who possess actual knowledge of public affairs; beware of those soothing the populace for private gain.
